etymology: Also the either-or fallacy: the Greek dilemma names two horns, and the trick is to admit only two.
committed_when: A decision is framed as a choice between the speaker's option and a disaster.
tell: The sentence has exactly two branches, and one of them is unthinkable.
counter: Name the third option out loud. A dilemma dies the moment a listener can see a door in the wall.
senses: Presenting a choice between two options when more exist, so that refusing one is treated as choosing the other.
It works by shrinking the field. Most real disputes have a third, boring option - wait, fund it differently, do half of it - and the boring option is exactly what the dilemma is built to hide.
example: *“You are either with us or with the terrorists.”* There is a third position - a citizen with a question about the evidence - and the sentence has just made it unsayable.

confused_with.tell: The dilemma collapses the field to two; equivalence claims those two weigh the same.
